title: Hybrid Spot/Reserved GPU Capacity — Experimentation Plan & Runbook
content:
Purpose
-----
This doc lays out a pragmatic experiment to blend spot/interruptible instances (cloud) with reserved/dedicated capacity (committed or Dedicated offering) to reduce cost while preserving latency SLOs and availability for Redwood customer workloads. It is a runbook + analysis template we can run in a region (primary candidate: us-west1) and then scale to eu-west1 if successful.

Background + motivation
-----------------------
- Current approach: conservative reserved capacity planning with 25–30% headroom across regions. High cost during idling and burst windows.
- Opportunity: run a hybrid model where non-latency-critical background workloads use spot capacity, and user-facing latency-sensitive routes use reserved/GPU-persistent pools.
- Risk: spot interruptions during peak inbound traffic could cascade to latency SLO violations. We need a safe, measurable experiment with clear abort criteria.

Goals
-----
1) Validate that a 20–35% substitution of reserved capacity with spot instances reduces per-token unit cost by >= 12% for selected workload slices.
2) Maintain 99.5% P50 latency SLO for chosen routes and <= 0.1% increase in error rate attributable to capacity changes.
3) Create an operational runbook for rapid scaling-down of spot-backed capacity and fallback to reserved pools in <90s.

Hypothesis
----------
If we route low-priority async batch and embedding creation tasks to spot instance pools and hold fast on reserved pools for interactive requests, then average per-GPU utilization will increase and our monthly GPU spend decreases, without measurable impact on user-facing latency.

Experiment scope and constraints
-------------------------------
- Regions: us-west1 primary, eu-west1 dry-run later.
- SKU candidates: A100-80GB (prod), A100-40GB (cost favorable), H100-80GB (reserved heavy).
- Workloads targeted: embeddings-batch, offline-indexing, nightly-retraining tasks, low-cost reranking, and fraction of non-async hosting for long-context jobs. Not voice/video pipelines.
- Timebox: 8 weeks (2 weeks ramp, 4 weeks steady-state, 2 weeks analysis + rollback).

Data inputs required
--------------------
- Per-region SKU lead times (procurement and cloud spot eviction history) — last 12 months
- Trace of route-level latency and QPS for past 30d (by model and route)
- Utilization histogram by instance type for last 30d
- Cost per-hour per-SKU (on-demand, reserved, spot) by region

Assumptions and safe defaults
-----------------------------
- Safe substitution initial cap: 25% of non-latency-critical reserved capacity.
- Max tolerated spot eviction rate during steady-state: 1.5% daily across chosen pool.
- Fallback target: on detection of rising P99 latency beyond 1.2x baseline for >3 consecutive 1m windows, trigger automatic drain of spot tasks and spin up reserved capacity fallback; target recovery <90s for traffic-critical routes.
- Billing amortization: reserved capacity cost accounted monthly; savings measured as delta of blended spend vs baseline committed+on-demand baseline.

SKU mix candidate matrix (quick snapshot)
----------------------------------------
- A100-80GB: baseline prod. Good for long-context gen; low eviction risk on reserved. Attr cost: high.
- A100-40GB (spot-friendly): lower cost, good for embeddings/batching; preemption tolerant.
- H100-80GB: premium for high-throughput low-latency; keep as reserved for top-tier customers.

Procurement and lead time considerations
--------------------------------------
- For reserved/Dedicated commitments, procurement lead time (internal ordering + cloud quota lead time) is modeled at 21–60 days depending on SKU and region. We will target a rolling 30-day procurement buffer for any planned capacity increase >10% sustained.
- Spot eviction lead times: collect historical daily eviction spikes; plan triggers to de-risk evection storms (e.g., cloud maintenance windows, new region promotion events).

Procurement triggers (experiment specific)
-----------------------------------------
- Trigger A: 7-day rolling average utilization >82% sustained AND projected 30-day demand growth >8% → open procurement request for +10% reserved capacity for SKU X in region Y (lead time window starts). Create PO template and involve finance.
- Trigger B: sudden sustained job backpressure (queue growth > 2000 pending jobs for 10m) → temporarily increase spot capacity by auto-scaling policy, but enable stricter eviction monitoring and shorten fallback cooldown to 30s.
- Manual override: SRE/infra on-call can flip a manual global “spot-safe” toggle in Console to migrate traffic to reserved-only mode.

Autoscaling and routing policy changes
-------------------------------------
- Implement two affinity pools per region: reserved-pool (pinned routes) and spot-pool (tagged workloads). Use smart-routing policy to retry on spot eviction with exponential backoff and immediate fallback to reserved pool for interactive calls.
- Batching controller: conservative batch sizes for spot-pool to limit the cost of preempted in-flight work. Ensure checkpointing for multi-step flows.

Monitoring & KPIs
------------------
- Cost KPIs: blended cost per token/day by region (compare baseline vs experiment), percent reduction in marginal GPU spend.
- Reliability KPIs: route-level P50/P95/P99 latencies, error rates, failed-inference retries count attributed to spot interruptions.
- Operational KPIs: time-to-fallback (median), number of manual interventions, frequency of spot eviction-induced rollbacks.
- Safety gates: if P99 for any critical route rises >1.5x baseline for >15 minutes, automated rollback to reserved-only occurs.

Runbook (steps for preflight -> ramp -> steady -> rollback)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Preflight (days -7 to 0):
- Validate dataset of eviction history and instantiate small test pool in us-west1.
- Create Linear tickets: ENGINFRA-482 (experiment), SRE-742 (oncall watch).
- Deploy metric dashboards: experiment overview, route heatmap, eviction timeline.
- Finance: register anticipated monthly savings and confirm budget for potential spot-driven transient costs.

Ramp (days 0–14):
- Week 0–1: route 10% of non-critical batch QPS to spot-pool. Watch KPIs. Daily sync with SRE.
- Week 1–2: if stable, increase to 25%. Run chaos schedule: induce small eviction waves (simulated) to test fallback.

Steady (weeks 3–6):
- Maintain 25–35% substitution. Collect cost and latency samples. Run two scheduled full-fallback drills to validate <90s recovery.

Rollback (criteria + steps):
- Auto rollback triggers: KPI gates or eviction > threshold. Steps: 1) set spot-safe=false; 2) instruct autoscaler to remove spot pool; 3) spin up reserved nodes via pre-warmed templates; 4) monitor until KPIs return to baseline; 5) create incident doc and postmortem.

Open questions / unknowns
------------------------
- How correlated are spot eviction windows across SKUs and regions? If correlation is high, hybrid strategy gains less.
- API throttling on cloud provider side when massing fallback to reserved pools — need to test quota headroom.
- Accounting model: how to fairly attribute reserved vs spot cost to customer tiers for billing transparency?

Next steps (owners + near term tasks)
------------------------------------
- Aisha (owner): prepare test cluster + dashboards by 2025-11-10.
- Marcus: write initial autoscaler policy + routing changes (ENGINFRA-489) by 2025-11-12.
- Diego: collect spot eviction history & region SKU lead times by 2025-11-07.
- Ruth/Omar: run two failover drills in staging and capture timing by 2025-11-18.

Appendix: quick example calc (expected monthly savings)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Baseline: 100 reserved A100-80GB nodes at $X/hr (assume $3.50/hr equivalent) = 100 * 24 * 30 * 3.5 = $252,000/mo.
- Hybrid: substitute 25 nodes with spot A100-40GB at $0.9/hr effective = reserved 75 * 3.5 + spot 25 * 0.9 = (75*3.5*24*30) + (25*0.9*24*30) = 189,000 + 16,200 = 205,200 -> savings ~18.6% (~$46,800/mo).
- Sensitivity: if eviction-driven rework increases CPU overhead by 2%, and that translates to 5% additional infra spend, net savings still >10% according to this example.

Notes-to-self style items (working doc flavor)
-----------------------------------------------
- Need a short customer comms plan if we ever test this on customer-visible fleets (esp. enterprise Dedicated tenants).
- Consider hybrid contractual language for Reserved + Spot fallback in enterprise proposals.
- Ticket cleanup: link all tickets in postmortem and tag appropriately.

End of doc.
